meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law for Québec private law (Civil Code of Québec) and Common Law for federal criminal and constitutional matters; Québec public and regulatory law follows the French civil tradition.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against FINTRAC, Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions, UN Security Council resolutions, the Criminal Code terrorist list, and relevant OFAC/SDN lists for any USD payment rails; politically exposed persons require enhanced due diligence, identification of source of funds, and senior-legal-approval before onboarding in accordance with PCMLTFR sections 11.2 and 11.3.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Portail officiel des services en ligne (recherche et réservation de nom)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All business names must be in French unless a recognized trademark exemption applies; the name must be grammatically correct and written in the Latin alphabet with French phonological transliteration standards, in conformity with the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is refused, the applicant may file a written review application with the Registraire des entreprises within 60 days of the refusal notice; the registrar will re-examine the decision. If the registrar confirms the rejection, judicial review may be sought before the Court of Québec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Reservations can be renewed by filing a new online request; there is no statutory extension beyond the original reservation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable for a low-risk design-subscription agency only if combined with a dedicated physical establishment address in Québec for service of process; a P.O. box alone is prohibited, and a shared co-working or domiciliation address must be operational during Québec business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10% likelihood of an unannounced registrar, FINTRAC, or tax-authority spot audit during the first three years; on-site inspections are rare for a standard design-services entity but may be triggered by low-tax jurisdiction indicators or inconsistent filing records.

P-44.1, arts. 1-19 (declaration of registration); Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c. CCQ-1991, arts. 2292-2294 (société en commandite / limited partnership), arts. 2186-2236 (partnership generally); Regulation respecting the fees payable under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) of a société en commandite (limited partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Civil Code of Québec imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement for a limited partnership (CA_LP, CA-QC); capital contributions are determined contractually in the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the general partner: (1) The Partnership adopts its Limited Partnership Agreement; the general partner subscribes to its interest with the capital contribution schedule set out therein, no statutory minimum paid-up capital being applicable under the Civil Code of Québec; (2) the registered office is fixed at the partnership's principal establishment in Montreal, Province of Québec, and a declaration of registration shall be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; (3) the general partner is appointed sole manager, authorized to execute all filing instruments, open bank accounts, and onboard Stripe Billing and Wise payment rails; (4) the secretary shall issue registration confirmations to all limited partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online name reservation service (Centre de services aux entreprises, Mon espace entreprises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request for the limited partnership through the Registraire's online portal. The proposed name must include a distinctive element, a descriptive or generic element, and a legal designation such as 'S.E.C.' or 'société en commandite'. The Registraire issues a name reservation certificate valid for 90 days if the name is admissible.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application
Requested corporate name (including legal designation)
Description of principal activities (ISIC 7410 design services)
Contact details of the applicant and general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused in a notice of inadmissibility, revise the distinctive element or add an additional distinctive component and resubmit the application within 15 days, or request a reconsideration by the Registraire with supporting justification and no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private drafting; optional notarization before a notary of the Chambre des notaires du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the convention de société en commandite identifying the general partner (full liability) and limited partners (liability capped at contributed capital), capital contribution schedule, profit allocation, management authority, withdrawal and transfer provisions, and dissolution events. Execute the agreement in counterpart; notarization is required only if real property is contributed, but is recommended for bank onboarding.
required_dossiers: Draft limited partnership agreement (convention de société en commandite)
Certified identification documents of all general and limited partners
Schedule of capital contributions and ownership percentages
Declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership for AML verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Disputes among partners on terms are cured by unanimous written amendment of the agreement before registration; no public authority intervention applies. Re-execute the agreement with corrected terms and re-present to the bank or registry as applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the declaration of registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Mon espace entreprises (online registration portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the déclaration d'immatriculation for the société en commandite through the Registraire's electronic filing system. State the partnership's name, principal establishment address in Quebec, general partner's identity and address, limited partners' aggregate contributions, and the partnership's activities. Pay the statutory registration fee by credit card or debit.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate (valid at filing date)
Completed online declaration of registration
Limited partnership agreement (certified copy)
Identification and Quebec address of the general partner
List of limited partners and aggregate contribution amounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a notice of query or refusal, cure by submitting a corrected declaration within 30 days of the notice, providing any missing supporting documents, and paying the applicable corrective filing fee; once cured, the registration is retroactive to the original filing date unless the law provides otherwise.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and Quebec QST/GST registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online) and Revenu Québec (Mon dossier d'entreprise)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the issued Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), register the partnership for a federal Business Number (BN) with the CRA and for Quebec QST and federal GST/HST with Revenu Québec. The limited partnership is a separate person for GST/QST purposes. Apply for the accounts to be effective from the commencement of commercial activities.
required_dossiers: Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and declaration of registration
Legal name and principal establishment address
Designated contact person of the general partner
Bank account details for refund and remittance purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or suspended, contact the CRA Business Window or Revenu Québec to reconcile identity data, correct any mismatched names or addresses, and resubmit the account activation request by fax or online rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal general operating permit and office occupancy clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ville de Montréal — Service de la mise en valeur du territoire (Permis et inspections)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the municipal application for a general business operating permit covering the partnership's leased office space used for UI/UX design subscription activities. Provide proof of the right of occupancy, a description of the office activities, and confirmation that no industrial processes are conducted. The City issues the permit after verifying building code conformity.
required_dossiers: Completed municipal permit application (Demande de permis)
Copy of the lease or proof of occupancy
Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and declaration of registration
Site layout plan and description of office use
Certificate of conformity from the building inspection service, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is refused due to non-conformity of the premises, obtain a corrective certificate from a licensed engineer or architect, rectify the identified defects, and resubmit the application with the fact-sheet to the Service de la mise en valeur du territoire within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of the partnership register and annual compliance calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partnership's registered office; monitored by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the internal limited partnership register containing the names and contribution schedules of all limited partners, the general partner's resolutions, and copies of the declaration of registration. Update the public declaration with the Registraire within 30 days of any change of name, address, general partner, or partners' contributions, and pay the annual declaration fee each year before the anniversary deadline.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the declaration of registration
Register of limited partners with capital contributions
General partner's resolutions and appointment instruments
Annual declaration calendar and fee schedule reminder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual declaration is late, a penalty is imposed by the Registraire; cure by filing the overdue declaration and paying the penalty plus arrears. Where a third party challenges the partnership's standing due to a lapse, the partnership may file a retroactive declaration with the Registraire's permission, subject to applicable fines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No specialized industrial licensing authority applies; general supervision by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and municipal permitting by Ville de Montréal — Service de la mise en valeur du territoire
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory sectoral license required for ISIC 7410 (product interface design and design-as-a-service); only the municipal general operating permit (permis d'exploitation) and occupancy clearance are applicable

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — pure office and administrative use with no industrial installations; no activities listed in section 2 of the Regulation respecting the environmental impact assessment and review of certain projects (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 23) and no Schedule I or II industrial process
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office occupancy only: no industrial wastewater discharge; sanitary wastewater is discharged exclusively to the municipal sewer system in compliance with Ville de Montréal by-laws; negligible volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, below the reporting thresholds of the Regulation respecting mandatory reporting of certain emissions of contaminants into the atmosphere (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 15); residual materials managed under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of residual materials (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 46) with low-risk office waste streams.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Service de sécurité incendie de Montréal (SIM) attesting to building occupancy load, alarm systems, emergency exits, and annual sprinkler inspections; occupational health and safety clearance under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c. S-2.1) administered by the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST); structural load certificate by a licensed engineer confirming that the floor rating supports the intended office equipment and furniture of the lease premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — federal GST/HST, Business Number (BN) and federal income tax administration, portal: canada.ca/en/revenue-agency and Business Registration Online (bro.businessregistration.gc.ca); Revenu Québec — Quebec Sales Tax (QST), provincial income tax and Numéro d'entreprise du Québec (NEQ), portal: revenuquebec.ca and clicSÉQUR Affaires; the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca) issues the NEQ and registers the société en commandite (limited partnership). Non-resident intake channel: CRA International Tax Services Office (1-800-959-5525) and the Non-Resident Business Account program.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the 10-digit NEQ (Quebec enterprise number), appointing a nominal representative if the LP carries on business in Quebec. Step 2: Apply for the 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) via CRA Business Registration Online, activating the GST/HST program account (RT), and where relevant payroll (RP) and income tax (RC) accounts. Step 3: Register with Revenu Québec for QST through clicSÉQUR Affaires, either upon exceeding the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold or immediately where the LP has a permanent establishment in Quebec and makes or intends to make taxable supplies to non-residents. Step 4: File the annual partnership information return (T5013) with CRA and issue T5013 slips to resident and non-resident partners; a foreign general partner must also complete the CRA non-resident registration and, for treaty-protected income, file Form NR301 to reduce Part XIII withholding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent under Income Tax Act section 96; the partnership itself pays no federal or Quebec income tax and each partner is allocated its pro rata share of income or loss for the fiscal period. The Specified Investment Flow-Through (SIFT) partnership rules would impose entity-level tax only if the LP's units were listed on a designated stock exchange, which is not the case for this private design-subscription LP. For GST/QST the LP is treated as a separate 'person' registrant carrying on a commercial activity, and for Quebec civil law the LP has separate patrimony for creditor claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election; classification follows the Income Tax Act and Quebec civil law. Available statutory elections relevant to this CA_LP: (1) single-registrant election for qualifying partnerships under Excise Tax Act section 272.1, with the mirror election under the Act respecting the Quebec sales tax, consolidating GST/HST and QST returns of the partners and the partnership; (2) non-resident partner net-basis election under Income Tax Act section 216 to replace 25% gross Part XIII withholding with tax on net Canadian-source income; (3) partnership fiscal period election under Income Tax Act section 249.1; (4) group or joint election under ETA section 273 or 274 for closely related registrants where the corporate general partner qualifies; (5) hybrid mismatch rules: Canada imposes the Part I.2 25% excessive entitlement tax and Income Tax Act section 18.4 rules on hybrid mismatch arrangements involving a foreign tax-indifferent partner; a US LLC partner cannot extend its check-the-box classification to the Canadian LP, and treaty tie-breaker rules govern dual-resident status rather than the US Section 7701 election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax, VAT-type, Excise Tax Act, federal GST at 5%) plus QST (Quebec Sales Tax at 9.975%, VAT-type, administered by Revenu Quebec, Act respecting the Quebec sales tax); combined Quebec consumption tax burden of 14.975% on domestic taxable supplies, with export supplies of services and digital intangibles zero-rated at 0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold under ETA section 240(1) and QSTA, calculated over the current calendar quarter plus the four preceding calendar quarters on taxable (non-zero-rated) supplies made in Canada/Linked Quebec supplies. Mandatory registration without reliance on the threshold applies when the LP is a non-resident partnership or carries on business in Canada through a permanent establishment in Quebec and makes taxable supplies; registration is also required for a registrant that makes zero-rated export supplies, because the LP must be registered to claim input tax credits / input tax refunds on its Canadian inputs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping or mandatory tax-clearing API regime is currently in force in Canada or Quebec for the 2025 filing period. Canada has adopted a voluntary Peppol-based Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework (pilot from 2024-2025 with the federal government as anchor buyer); Quebec enacted Bill 37 (LQ 2024, c. 18) amending the Tax Administration Act and the QSTA to introduce mandatory B2B/B2C e-invoicing and e-reporting, to be phased in by government regulation, with large taxpayers expected around 2026-2028 and SMEs later. Current compliance obligations: GST/HST returns via GST/HST NETFILE or the GST/HST return XML/API; QST returns and remittances via clicSÉQUR Affaires web services; invoices to Quebec-based clients must be in French under the Charter of the French Language (as amended effective 1 June 2025) and must show the BN, the QST registration number, and the zero-rating annotation TPS/TVQ 0% for export supplies to non-residents.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The UI/UX design subscription (ISIC 7410 / NAICS 541430, design-as-a-service) qualifies for zero-rating under Schedule VI, Part V, sections 7 and 10 of the Excise Tax Act where: (1) the recipient is a non-resident of Canada, not an individual present in Canada at the time the supply is made; (2) the service is not in connection with real or immovable property situated in Canada; (3) the service is not in connection with corporeal moveable property situated in Canada; and (4) the service is not supplied to an individual for personal consumption while in Canada. Services performed partly or wholly in Canada for a non-resident client are zero-rated as supplies made to a non-resident; services rendered wholly outside Canada are additionally zero-rated on a territorial basis. The QST applies the same 0% rate for supplies of services and intangible property made to persons that are not Quebec residents and that are not recipients in Quebec. Because the export supplies are taxable at 0% (not exempt), the registered LP may claim full input tax credits and input tax refunds on Canadian software, payroll, hosting and professional-fee expenses. Canada imposes no statutory 180-day foreign-currency repatriation window: export proceeds may be received in CAD or foreign currency, converted under CRA published exchange rates, and the CRA verifies place of supply, non-resident status and provision of the service rather than the date of funds receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) filed via the Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) system — mandatory only if physical design deliverables or prototypes are exported; pure digital design subscriptions are intangible supplies outside the customs declaration regime
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (for couriered physical prototypes, design kits or printed deliverables, evidencing physical departure from Canada)

Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103 or Canadian bank credit confirmation) or the Stripe_Billing / Wise foreign-currency payout ledger evidencing inward cross-border payment and the non-resident payer identity

International design subscription agreement (MSA / SOW / terms of service) identifying the non-resident recipient, place of supply, Canadian design performance scope, and absence of Canadian real-property and movable-property nexus, together with French-language zero-rated invoices
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no 180-day FX repatriation deadline for export zero-rating, but CRA and Revenu Quebec can reassess a zero-rated export claim if the supply is re-characterized as domestic, causing clawback of unpaid GST at 5% and QST at 9.975% plus daily compounded prescribed arrears interest (approximately 9% regular and 14% corporate arrears in 2025). Penalties include: (i) ETA section 285 false-statement penalty of the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the net tax understated; (ii) ETA section 280 willful-evasion penalty of 50% of the total tax sought, fines up to CAD 25,000 per count on summary conviction or CAD 100,000 on indictment, and imprisonment up to two years; (iii) Quebec gross-negligence penalty under the Tax Administration Act (Quebec) of 50% of unreported QST; (iv) Income Tax Act section 163(2) gross-negligence penalty of 50% applied to the partners' understated income where the export zero-rating substantiation is fraudulent or false; and (v) CRA Export Verification Program and Revenu Quebec post-export audits, which may suspend or claw back input tax credit / input tax refund claims. The CRA may also impose Director/Officer liability and joint-and-several liability on the general partner. Mitigation requires retention of the full documentation bundle for at least six years, attested non-resident status certification (Form NR301 where applicable), and French-language invoicing compliant with Quebec Bill 96 amendments effective 1 June 2025.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), Ottawa; exchange-control and monetary policy coordination rests with the Minister of Finance and the Department of Finance Canada; AML/transactional supervision is exercised by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), while the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) regulates Quebec-regulated money-services businesses and Desjardins.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction with full current-account and capital-account convertibility. The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a free-floating currency; there is no exchange-control law, no licensing regime, and no central-bank pre-approval for profit repatriation, capital contributions, or partnership distributions to non-resident limited partners. CAD/USD/EUR subscription receipts (Stripe and Wise settlements) and equity injections may be retained in foreign-currency accounts without mandatory conversion. Operational hurdles are limited to (i) FINTRAC large-value reporting obligations imposed on the bank for cross-border electronic fund transfers at or above CAD 10,000, and (ii) federal and Quebec income-tax withholding on the Canadian-source taxable allocation to non-resident partners; neither constitutes an FX convertibility barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None exist in Canada. There is no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation quota for export proceeds derived from design-subscription services (ISIC 7410 / NAICS 541430). The CA_LP may hold foreign currency indefinitely in USD/EUR-denominated treasury accounts, subject only to an income-tax functional-currency election under subsection 261(2) of the Income Tax Act if the primary record-keeping currency is other than CAD.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec (Mouvement Desjardins), Lévis/Montréal
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD) and segregated Capital Escrow sub-account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada), Montréal
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD/USD dual-currency) and Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), Montréal commercial office

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for settlement aggregation and low-value disbursements; Low for primary treasury custody. Wise (Wise Payments Canada Inc.) is registered as a money-services business (MSB) with FINTRAC and, for Quebec activity, with the AMF; it is not a Schedule I/II bank and deposits are not insured by CDIC or the Fonds de sécurité des dépôts du Québec. Legal constraints: (i) no EMI passport exists in Canada, so Wise may not offer deposit-taking, credit, or constructed ISDA FX lines; (ii) funds held at Wise are not protected by a statutory trust or insolvency ring-fence equivalent to bank depositor preference; (iii) Wise executes FX as principal at its own mid-market spread, creating counterparty price risk inconsistent with audited treasury policy. Wise Business is nonetheless operationally viable as a secondary rail for aggregating Stripe payouts and paying small Canadian contractors below CAD 25,000 per transaction; it must not hold capital escrow funds or partnership distribution proceeds above the large-transaction monitoring threshold.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A limited partnership has no directors; the General Partner (GP) and all partners holding 25% or more of the LP must be identified. Canadian Schedule I banks permit fully remote onboarding for Canadian-resident individual and corporate GPs using dual-process electronic identity verification and REQ certificate verification; a video interview is normally required for first-time bank relationships. Where the GP is non-resident, an in-branch interview or notarized identity attestation (with legalization or apostille) is typically mandated. Non-resident limited partners are not required to appear in person if the GP is identifiable and the certified partnership register is provided. The statutory basis is the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, which permit electronic identification subject to the bank's red-flag assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through entity opacity: inability to identify ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) of the Limited Partnership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Partnership Agreement (Convention de société) listing every partner's full legal name, date of birth, residential address, ownership percentage, and capital contribution; updated Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) extract showing registered office and the GP; a UBO organizational chart signed by each 25%-plus partner; a declarations page confirming no nominee shareholders, bare trustees, or bearer interests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners and recurring inbound subscription revenue creating unexplained cross-border flow patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from Quebec counsel confirming limited partnership law, partner liability, and non-resident tax status; 24-month business projection aligning projected wire frequency with a Design_As_A_Service subscription model; active website and client invoices evidencing ISIC 7410 / NAICS 541430 operations; a statement of source of wealth and source of funds for each non-resident partner, with bank references for accounts funding the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment aggregator taint: deposits via Stripe and Wise perceived as mixed commercial funds or undisclosed intermediation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed Payment Processor Agreements with Stripe and Wise; merchant account confirmations and payout schedules; monthly processor reports mapping subscriber identities to invoices; written treasury policy restricting processor balances to settlement-only and mandating daily sweep to the Schedule I operating account; chargeback and refund policy documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly formed LP with no trading track record or prior banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Declaration of Registration (Immatriculation) filed with the REQ; pro-forma financial statements; GP's personal and corporate bank references; evidence of business substance (registered office lease, insurance certificates, contractor agreements); executed partner capital call notices evidencing committed funding.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from non-resident limited partners: route as a SWIFT MT103 credit transfer to the CA_LP segregated Capital Escrow Account at National Bank of Canada or Desjardins, with beneficiary line identifying the LP's REQ number and the capital-call notice number; use the bank's then-current 4-digit wire purpose code for direct-investment capital contributions (equity injection into a Canadian enterprise, not a loan). A non-resident partner establishing a new Canadian business must also file the Investment Canada Act new-business notification with ISED within 30 days of establishment (no substantive review because the design-subscription business is non-cultural and below WTO enterprise-value thresholds). Subscription revenue: Stripe_Billing settlements enter Payments Canada clearing and are credited to the operational account via the bank's automated clearing/electronic transfer rail; Wise payouts arrive as aggregated EFT credits with a payment-reference memo. Verification protocol: (i) reconcile each Notification of Credit (NoC) against the Stripe payout report or the capital-call schedule; (ii) confirm FINTRAC large-EFT reporting obligation rests on the bank, not the LP; (iii) maintain a transaction log separating escrowed partner capital from operating receipts; (iv) convert no FX at the processor if the bank account is dual-currency — instead sweep processor balances in original currency and execute a single treasury forward.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Contractor and vendor payments outside Canada: SWIFT MT103 with purpose code mapped to the Statistics Canada international-payments classification for business/professional and computer services (design subcontracting) or, for non-resident partner profit distributions, the code for distributed earnings of direct investment (FDI income). Domestic CAD disbursements: same-day electronic funds transfer through Payments Canada ACSS clearing, or LVTS/Lynx high-value wire for amounts above CAD 50,000, using the beneficiary's 9-digit Canadian routing number (institution-transit) rather than an IBAN. Wise batch transfers are allowed only for payments below CAD 25,000 where immediate finality is not critical; the primary rail remains direct bank wire to preserve audit trail and to avoid the bank's large-transaction monitoring flags. Commercial letters of credit are unnecessary and inappropriate: the underlying transactions are intangible service subscriptions (design-as-a-service), not documentary sales of goods; use neither LC nor documentary collection, and prohibit open-account terms except for established enterprise clients.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forward contracts (CAD vs USD and CAD vs EUR) with a Schedule I Canadian bank or Desjardins, documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a long-form FX confirmation, executed solely against documented subscription receivable exposure with no speculative trading.
FX swaps under the 1998 FX and Currency Option Definitions for short-term recycling of USD subscription cash into CAD operating liquidity without creating an uncovered forward position.
European-style FX options (strangle or risk-reversal structures) for asymmetric protection of USD-denominated recurring revenue subject to board-approved maximum net-open-position limits.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps are legally permissible but economically unjustified at the projected balance-sheet size; NDFs are legally available for CAD but are not market practice because the Canadian dollar is fully convertible and a deliverable currency — the CA_LP should avoid non-deliverable structures and use deliverable forwards instead.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Enterprise Registration Declaration (déclaration annuelle de mise à jour)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the anniversary date of the partnership's initial registration, regardless of whether registry information has changed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration exposes the partnership to prescribed late fees and interest; continued non-compliance may result in notice from the registrar, cancellation of registration, and loss of legal publicity benefits for the partnership and its general partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (T5013) for the federal income tax period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal period, on or before March 31 of the next calendar year; for a non-calendar fiscal period, no later than three months after the fiscal period end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties under section 162 of the Income Tax Act apply, including a minimum CAD 100 penalty, a maximum CAD 2,500 penalty, daily penalty amounts for continuing default, and possible prosecution for willful non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GST/HST and QST returns, where the partnership has elected annual filing frequency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CRA for GST/HST and Revenu Québec for QST
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the third calendar month after the partnership's fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the annual deadline is March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or omissions attract a 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months, statutory interest, and higher penalties or prosecution for habitual or deliberate non-compliance; no registry strike-off consequence arises from sales tax defaults.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a non-public, non-reporting-issuer Quebec limited partnership under the Civil Code of Québec or the Income Tax Act; audit obligations arise only from partnership agreement provisions, lender or investor covenants, or securities-law reporting status, not from revenue or asset thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP under the CPA Canada Handbook; IFRS is compulsory for publicly accountable enterprises, while ASPE (Part II) is available for a private limited partnership; no Quebec-specific financial reporting framework supersedes these standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec's legal publicity regime requires the annual declaration to identify the general partners and, where the partnership is subject to significant-control disclosure, every individual with significant control, generally direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more of the partnership interests or equivalent control. Transfers of partnership interests must be recorded internally, reflected in the next annual declaration, and cross-matched to the T5013 allocation schedule filed with CRA; there is no separate federal UBO filing for a limited partnership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (all general and limited partners with contribution, withdrawal, and profit-allocation records)
Register of Persons with Significant Control (where applicable under Quebec legal publicity rules)
Minute Book and written resolutions of the partners and management committee

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 900 per year for a registered office and corporate agent in Montreal or Quebec City, including annual registry declaration preparation and document coordination
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 6,000 per year for a design-subscription limited partnership with a simple partner structure if an independent audit or review is contractually required; no statutory minimum audit fee applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (combined federal 15% and Quebec 11.5% active business income rate for a Canadian-controlled private corporation, before refundable dividend tax treatment; general federal rate 15% plus Quebec 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) claiming the small business deduction: net federal rate 9% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income (reduced by the Quebec provincial abatement and subject to provincial deduction phase-out), and Quebec rate reduced to 3.2% on the same band (Quebec small business deduction), resulting in a combined effective rate of approximately 12.2% on eligible active business income up to the business limit. Additional incentives include the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credit (35% refundable for CCPCs on qualified expenditures up to CAD 3,000,000), the Quebec Research and Development Tax Credit (14% refundable on eligible salaries, with possible 30% for certain university or public research centre contracts), the Quebec film or multimedia production tax credits, and the Quebec equity tax credit for cooperative investment. Interest deductibility on debt finance, capital cost allowance deductions, and eligible capital property treatment apply under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Quebec Taxation Act.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed via the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) GST Filing Internet Gateway or third-party E-file software; Quebec: Corporations Tax Return (CO-17) filed via Revenu Québec’s electronic transmission service (EDITION) or approved E-file software. The T2 return must include the relevant schedules (e.g., Schedule 1 – Active Business Income, Schedule 4 – Corporation Calculations, Schedule 50 – Shareholder Information) and Quebec CO-17 schedules as applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; instalments of corporate income tax are generally required quarterly (monthly or quarterly) based on the corporation's tax year, and GST/QST returns are filed annually, quarterly, or monthly depending on threshold registrations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Federal T2 due date: within six months after the end of the taxation year (e.g., for a December 31 year-end, due June 30 of the following calendar year). Balance of taxes due: two months after the end of the taxation year (three months for certain Canadian-controlled private corporations that are eligible for the refundable dividend tax credit or that have cumulative taxable capital of less than CAD 15,000,000). Quebec CO-17 due date: within six months after the end of the taxation year. Payment deadline for Quebec income tax: generally the same two-month or three-month rule as federal. Installment payments are required in monthly or quarterly installments when net tax owing exceeds CAD 3,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification and mailing address of the corporation, fiscal year-end date, and Business Number (BN) / Quebec enterprise number (NEQ).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners must report their share of Canadian-source partnership income on their own tax filings. The T2 return must be prepared for the Canadian resident partnership (the limited partnership is not a distinct taxpayer for Canadian income tax purposes; the partnership files an information return (T5013 Summary and T5013 slips) to allocate income to partners). The partnership must provide each non-resident partner with T5013 slips reflecting the Canadian active business income share. The non-resident partner must file a Canadian non-resident income tax return (T1 or T2 as applicable) and may be subject to Part XIII withholding tax on distributions. The partnership information return must include each partner's name, address, and share of income and deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue and business income from the UI/UX design subscription services and any other active business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The limited partnership reports all Canadian and foreign business revenue. Revenue from design services is generally Canadian-source if generated through the Canadian permanent establishment (the partnership's business operations in Quebec). Non-resident partners do not directly report revenue on the T2; their allocable share flows through T5013.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advertising, design, software, administrative, and other operating expenses attributable to generating the design subscription income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be reasonable and incurred to earn income from the Canadian business. Non-resident partners cannot deduct personal expenses or expenses unrelated to the partnership. The partnership should track expenses in Canadian dollars and allocate to each partner in accordance with the partnership agreement. Cross-border management fees or service fees paid to related non-resident entities are subject to transfer pricing and Part XIII withholding tax rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries and wages paid to employees engaged in UI/UX design, project management, and administrative support.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The partnership must withhold Canadian payroll taxes (federal income tax, Quebec provincial income tax, Quebec Parental Insurance Plan, Employment Insurance, Quebec Pension Plan, and Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) assessment) for employees working in Quebec. Non-resident partners are not employees of the partnership and no payroll withholdings apply to their distributions, unless the partner works in Canada as an employee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Office costs, rent, utilities, software subscriptions, professional fees, insurance, and other administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The partnership may allocate a portion of general overhead to non-resident partners based on their profit-sharing ratio. Overhead expenses attributable to the Canadian business are deductible only if incurred for the purpose of earning income in Canada. Non-resident partners should ensure that the partnership maintains supporting invoices and contracts to substantiate all deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance (depreciation) claimed on tangible capital assets used in the business, such as computers, office equipment, and furniture.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The partnership computes capital cost allowance under the Canadian Income Tax Act and Quebec Taxation Act. Non-resident partners are not entitled to claim direct capital cost allowance on partnership assets; their share of the deduction flows through the T5013 and is reported on their own tax return, subject to their taxation status in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 – Schedule 1, Lines 400–499 (Federal) / CO-17 – Quebec Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of active business income, federal and Quebec small business deduction, provincial abatement, and any refundable dividend tax credit on investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The partnership's active business income is allocated among partners according to the partnership agreement. The small business deduction is generally only available to Canadian-resident private corporations that are CCPCs. A limited partnership that is not a CCPC may not itself claim the small business deduction; the deduction is claimed by Canadian-resident corporate partners on their proportionate share of the partnership's active business income. Non-resident corporate partners are generally not eligible for the small business deduction. The partnership should file T2 with the applicable schedules to allow resident corporate partners to claim their share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed information of each partner, including allocation percentages, partner type (individual, corporation, trust, partnership), jurisdiction of residence, and identification numbers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All partners, including non-resident individuals and corporations, must be identified on Schedule 8. Non-resident partners must provide the partnership with their foreign tax identification numbers and jurisdiction of residence. The partnership must also file an annual T5013 (Partnership Information Return) with CRA and a corresponding Quebec Relevé 15 with Revenu Québec, reporting each partner's share of income, deductions, and tax credits. Failure to report non-resident partners may result in penalties and Part XIII withholding obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before considering loss carryovers and other adjustments, after deducting non-capital losses from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Partnership losses may be allocated to a non-resident partner only to the extent of that partner's limited partnership at-risk amount. A non-resident limited partner cannot deduct partnership losses exceeding their adjusted cost base in the partnership interest. Loss carryforward tracking is maintained at the partner level, not the partnership level, subject to the partner's own Canadian tax position.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under the Income Tax Act: 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months (maximum 17%), with increased penalties for repeat filings; late filing penalties for corporations with taxable capital exceeding CAD 1,000,000 are calculated differently (minimum penalty of CAD 500 per month, up to 24 months, capped at CAD 6,000). Revenu Québec late filing penalty: 5% of the balance due plus 0.5% per month, maximum penalty 20%; repeat failure penalties of 10% plus 2% per month (maximum 40%). Daily interest rates are applied by both CRA and Revenu Québec on overdue amounts, compounded daily; the prescribed rates are adjusted quarterly (CRA) and annually for Revenu Québec and currently approximate 4.9% to 6.9% annually. Failure to file T5013 or Relevé 15 information returns attracts penalties of CAD 25 per day up to a maximum of CAD 2,500 (or CAD 100 per day for deliberate omissions, max CAD 12,500). Personal liability of directors and, for partnerships, general partners: the CRA may assess directors for unremitted payroll and withheld amounts, and general partners are jointly and severally liable for partnership tax debts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory Canadian withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders is 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act. For a limited partnership distributing income to non-resident partners, the partnership must withhold 25% on the non-resident partner's share of partnership income that is taxable in Canada but not distributed, and on actual distributions of Canadian-source income, unless reduced by an applicable income tax treaty. Quebec does not impose a separate dividend withholding tax; the federal Part XIII rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a tax treaty, the non-resident partner or shareholder must complete and submit the applicable Canada Revenue Agency form: Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Convention) for treaty-based relief from Part XIII withholding on dividends, interest, royalties, or rental payments. The form must be provided to the Canadian payer (the limited partnership or the paying corporation) before the payment date, and the payer must confirm the partner's entitlement to the treaty benefit. For a partnership, the treaty claim is evaluated based on the partner's country of residence; the partner should provide a certificate of residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, evidencing residency. In the case of a limited partner resident in a treaty country (e.g., the U.S. LLC member, U.K. LLP, or Hong Kong corporate entity), the applicable treaty rate (typically 5% for substantial shareholding companies, 15% for portfolio dividends) applies. The partnership must attach Form NR301 to the T5013 returns or maintain it in its books. The withholding agent (the partnership or its general partner) is liable for any deficiency if the form is not obtained. For Quebec purposes, the same treaty relief is recognized under the Income Tax Conventions Act and the Quebec Taxation Act incorporates the federal treaty provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding rates: interest 25% (except for arm's-length interest on certain listed obligations, which is exempt), royalty payments for the use of or right to use any copyright, patent, trademark, or design 25%. Under the Canada–U.S. Tax Treaty, qualifying arm's-length interest is generally exempt (0%) and royalties qualify for 0% or 10% depending on the category (copyright royalties for cultural works are 0%, industrial royalties like design or software are typically 0% under the U.S. treaty due to the elimination of withholding in most cases, but certain patents may be 10%). Under the Canada–U.K. Tax Treaty, interest is generally exempt, and royalties are generally 10%. Under the Canada–Hong Kong Tax Agreement, interest is exempt, and royalties are generally 10% for industrial royalties. For UI/UX design subscription services, amounts paid for cross-border use of design assets or software user interfaces may be characterized as royalties if they are for the use of copyright in a design; pure service fees for design-as-a-service are generally business income, not royalties, and are not subject to Part XIII withholding unless they are a deemed Canadian-source payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada imposes transfer pricing documentation requirements on transactions between a Canadian resident taxpayer and non-resident related parties. The threshold is CAD 1,000,000 in gross revenues, gross expenditures, or both, for the taxation year, for transactions involving goods or services (including cross-border subscription and design service transactions). For transactions involving intangible property, the threshold is CAD 500,000. The documentation must include a Master File, Local File, and Country-by-Country Report (for which the local entity threshold is CAD 10,000,000 in revenue and related group revenue of CAD 1,050,000,000 for CBCR filing). Quebec adopts the federal transfer pricing rules under the Taxation Act; Revenu Québec does not impose a separate TP documentation threshold, but references federal TP rules. The partnership must prepare contemporaneous documentation if its related-party cross-border transactions exceed the CAD 1,000,000 threshold, and must ensure that all non-arm's-length transactions are priced at arm's length. Failure to provide documentation underlines a penalty: 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment, with a minimum penalty of CAD 5,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to the UAE or BVI frameworks, but the Canada Revenue Agency applies general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) under section 245 of the Income Tax Act and Quebec GAAR under section 1079.2 of the Quebec Taxation Act to deny tax benefits from transactions or arrangements that are primarily tax-motivated and that lack substantive business purpose. The limited partnership must demonstrate genuine business activity in Quebec (employees, offices, client contracts, and decision-making). Non-resident partners cannot use the Canadian limited partnership solely to access treaty benefits without substantial economic presence; the CRA may apply the treaty-shopping limitation (beneficial ownership and principal purpose test) under Canada's treaties, and the OECD multilateral instrument (MLI) where applicable. A limited partnership that lacks economic substance in Canada may be regarded as a conduit and the income recharacterized, exposing the non-resident partners to full 25% Part XIII withholding without treaty relief, or the Canada Revenue Agency may deny treaty benefits under anti-abuse provisions. The partnership must also comply with corporate veil requirements, maintain a registered office in Quebec, and file annual registrations (Registraire des entreprises) to reinforce economic substance. For transfer pricing, the partner's foreign entity must be afforded adequate economic substance; the documentation should confirm that any related-party cost-sharing arrangements (e.g., intercompany design services, licensing of design assets) reflect actual functions, assets, and risks in Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting partnership revenue from UI/UX design subscription contracts, underreporting Canadian-source income, creating fictitious invoices, or claiming ineligible deductions or tax credits (e.g., SR&ED claims for non-qualifying design work). Knowingly filing a false or wilfully evasive T2 return or T5013 slip.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal Income Tax Act: severe penalties of 50% of the federal tax evaded (gross negligence penalty), plus interest and civil penalties. Revenu Québec: penalty of 50% of the tax evaded for false statements or omissions; criminal prosecution for tax evasion (wilfully evading tax) is punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of 50% to 200% of the amount evaded (federal), and up to 18 months' imprisonment and fines up to 100% of the tax evaded under the Quebec Taxation Act. Civil fraud penalties may also apply. For a corporation, fines may be substantial; a false statement under the Income Tax Act carries a penalty of the greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the understated tax for the year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers of the general partner of the limited partnership are personally liable for unpaid withheld taxes (payroll deductions, GST/QST, Part XIII withholding) and for corporate tax debts if the corporation grossly neglects to remit. Criminal tax evasion may expose controlling minds to imprisonment up to 5 years, court-ordered restitution, and travel bans or seizures of assets. Civil liability also arises for participation in a fraud that causes loss to the Crown; the CRA may assess directors personally up to the amount of unremitted payroll or withholding tax. Quebec Revenue may similarly hold directors responsible for unpaid amounts and may pursue an investigative order against the corporate veil (lifting) when it is proved that the corporation is a sham or conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating the Canadian limited partnership as a pure shell with no business activities, without a Quebec registered office or employees, and routing all subscription payments directly to an offshore non-resident partner without reasonable economic substance in Canada. This can also include accumulating partnership losses and allocating them to high-wealth non-resident partners to shelter foreign income, or using the partnership to strip value from Canadian operations without arm's-length intercompany compensation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can disallow loss allocations, deny non-resident treaty benefits, recharacterize the arrangement as a sham, and assess unreported income at 25% Part XIII withholding on gross distributions. GAAR penalties (section 245) impose a 10% penalty on disallowed tax benefits in addition to reassessment. Civil penalties: up to CAD 12,500 for schedule filing omissions. In extreme cases, the partnership could be dissolved under Quebec civil law for nullity of a legal act made with illicit purpose. For non-resident partners, the CRA may impose an 25% withholding tax on all distributions and a 10% penalty. The Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec routinely exchange information on entities lacking substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners of a shell limited partnership may be liable for the company's tax liabilities under the Income Tax Act (director liability for GST/HST and payroll, section 227.1) and under Quebec laws (section 51 of the Taxation Act, and the Civil Code of Quebec). Courts may disregard the general partner's separate identity if the general partner is a mere puppet or is using the partnership to evade obligations; this permits principals to be held personally liable for all unpaid tax, penal interest, and fines. Travel bans under the Seized Property Management Act or the Criminal Code may apply if a criminal charge of fraud or money laundering is filed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting design-subscription payments without performing customer due diligence, failing to register with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as a money services business (MSB) or casino (not applicable to design agencies), but secondary AML red flags: making or accepting large cash payments (over CAD 10,000) without reporting, structuring payments to avoid reporting, or processing subscription payments for third-party clients that are falsely invoiced to obscure the identity of the beneficiary, particularly involving high-risk jurisdictions. Canada's Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act applies to reporting entities; a design agency is not a reporting entity unless it deals in virtual currency, money services, or precious metals. Nonetheless, failure to maintain an adequate AML compliance program when it is a financial intermediary or when it accepts third-party funding can constitute laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Criminal Code of Canada and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: money laundering is an indictable crime with imprisonment for life (maximum 10 years under section 462.31, with life for trafficking proceeds under related narcotics offences) and fines in the court's discretion; the Proceeds of Crime Act imposes administrative monetary penalties of up to CAD 1,000,000 for non-compliance by reporting entities (recent amendments allow FINTRAC to impose penalties of up to CAD 2,000,000 for non-compliance and CAD 500,000 for failure to submit a suspicious transaction report (STR)). In Quebec, the Financial Markets Tribunal may impose administrative penalties. Suspicious transactions connected to corruption or fraud can trigger seizure of property and restraint orders. For the corporate entity, a conviction may result in significant fines (unlimited for indictable offences) and restitution orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior officers and directors may face criminal liability for laundering proceeds of crime if they knowingly aided or directed transactions. Personal liability includes freezing orders over personal assets, confiscation of moveable/immovable property, travel bans restricting departure from Canada (under certain federal/Quebec orders), and imprisonment up to 10 years (life for related financing offences). Directors who turn a blind eye to suspicious transactions may be charged under the
